Catching What the
System Already Cleared.

Three real fraud detection cases from my 19-month tenure on the Rocket Companies account at TCS eServe. In each case, the file had already been reviewed and cleared before it reached me. My job was not just to process — it was to verify.

All cases described in professional terms consistent with my role. Customer-identifying details are not included — consistent with data privacy obligations.

Why I Caught Cases Others Missed — My Personal Standard
Most mortgage operations professionals verify what is in front of them — a document is present, a signature exists, a field is filled. That is surface-level verification. It catches simple errors. It does not catch fraud. My standard was different: every case went through three layers of verification regardless of whether a flag had been raised. Fraud is specifically designed to appear clean on the surface. The only way to know is to go deeper. This three-layer approach is what I applied to every single case across 19 months — not just suspicious ones.
Layer 01
Full-Field Review
Every field verified against its corresponding source — not just its presence, but its accuracy against county and government records simultaneously.
Layer 02
Multi-Source Cross-Check
Cross-referenced against at least two independent external sources. A discrepancy in one source can be a data entry error. A discrepancy across multiple is a flag.
Layer 03
Pattern Recognition
Compared each case against fraud patterns documented previously. Forged documents have consistent tells — formatting anomalies, name mismatches, notarisation errors — that recur.
Fraud Detection Case Studies
Case Type · Document Forgery
Forged Quit Claim Deed — Grantor Name Mismatch
Rocket Companies Account  ·  System status before my review: Cleared  ·  Detected during KYC / CDD screen
System: Cleared Outcome: Fraud Confirmed
Background
A routine ownership transfer request arrived in my queue — a Quit Claim Deed submitted to change the property owner on record. The system had processed it through standard validation checks and returned no flags. It was assigned to me for KYC review and account update processing.
What I Found
During my Layer 01 full-field review, the grantor name on the submitted Quit Claim Deed did not match the name on record in the county recorder database for the same property. The discrepancy was a single character off in the last name — close enough to pass an automated check, not close enough to be a legitimate match when cross-referenced against three independent county sources simultaneously.
Why It Was Missed
The system's validation checks verified that the document was present, properly formatted, and internally consistent. They were not designed to cross-reference the grantor name against external county recorder data — that step was a manual one. The document passed automated checks because it was formatted correctly and contained all required fields. The fraud was in the identity of the grantor, not the structure of the document.
What I Did
Stopped processing immediately. Compiled a full evidence document detailing every point of discrepancy with county record references. Coordinated joint review and double sign-off with the Rocket Companies client. Permanently closed the case, blocked it from re-entering the processing queue, and forwarded to the internal investigations team.
Case Type · Identity Fraud
Borrower Identity Mismatch Across Systems
Rocket Companies Account  ·  Pre-cleared at intake level before KYC review  ·  Detected during full CDD screen
Pre-Cleared at Intake Outcome: Fraud Confirmed
Background
A sensitive account update case arrived — the type that requires identity verification before any action. The intake process had confirmed that the customer contact details matched what was on file. The case was forwarded to me as ready for processing.
What I Found
My full CDD screen cross-referenced SSN, driver's licence details, and government records simultaneously. The SSN on the submitted identity document did not reconcile correctly across all three sources. In the mortgage servicing system it was associated with one identity profile. Cross-referenced against government verification channels, it returned a different name variant that matched neither the contact name nor the submitted ID document. No single system had caught this because each only compared within its own data.
Why It Was Missed
The intake check verified that the contact name matched what was on the account. It had not performed multi-source cross-verification of the SSN against external government records. The mismatch only existed at the intersection of internal and external data — a gap that only a manual, multi-source CDD process surfaces.
What I Did
Processing stopped immediately. Documented the SSN discrepancy in full — recording conflicting data from each source with references. Compiled evidence package, coordinated client sign-off. Permanently closed and blocked the case, forwarded to investigations.
Case Type · Cross-Customer Document Error / Fraud Attempt
Customer A Documents Attached to Customer B Account
Rocket Companies Account  ·  Passed QC at prior processing stage  ·  Detected during end-to-end case review
Prior QC: Passed Outcome: Blocked
Background
A case arrived that had already passed a prior processing stage and quality check. It appeared to be a routine account update with supporting documentation attached. Nothing in the case summary indicated a problem.
What I Found
During my end-to-end case review, the supporting documents attached to the account did not belong to the account holder on record. The identity documents, property records, and supporting materials corresponded to a completely different customer's account entirely. Names, property details, and account references in the attached documents did not match the account they had been filed against. This is a cross-customer document error — it can occur through system glitches, manual filing errors, or deliberate fraud where documents from one customer's file are used to support a transaction on another's account.
Why It Was Missed
The prior QC check had verified that documents were present and that document types matched what was required for the case type. It had not performed a full content cross-check — specifically borrower names, property addresses, and account references — against the account they were attached to. That level of content verification was not part of the standard prior-stage check.
What I Did
Halted processing and escalated immediately — to the Team Lead and directly to the Rocket client, given that cross-customer document errors have legal implications for both affected accounts. Documented the full discrepancy, identified which accounts were impacted, coordinated remediation for both. Both accounts reviewed, case blocked, forwarded to investigations.
